title: When Something Stops Working: Modes From Full Speed to a Safe Stop, a Second Fault That Costs More, and Coming Back Up One Step at a Time

questions.question: Why not just stop when anything fails?
options: A stopped vehicle uses more power
The checklist would refuse the next run
A vehicle that stops needs a person to walk to it, for a fault a slower vehicle could live with
questions.explanation: Most faults leave a vehicle that can still do something safely. Dropping to a slower mode keeps it working and saves the walk.

questions.question: A lost scanner asked for which mode?
options: 0, full: the other sensors cover it
questions.explanation: With no scanner nothing sees obstacles and the protective fields are blind, so no speed is safe.

questions.question: A lost GNSS and a lost link together asked for:
options: 2, a creep: a second fault costs more
questions.explanation: Either alone asks for reduced. Together, the vehicle has a poorer position and nobody to ask, and the mode drops a step further.

questions.question: A requirement flapping every 2 s changed the mode raw and through the manager:
questions.explanation: A worse requirement is taken at once and a better one only after 10 s of being better. The flapping never lasted that long, so the mode went down once and stayed.

questions.question: How long did the vehicle take to be back at full speed once the scanner came back?
options: At once: the fault had cleared
questions.explanation: Up is one step for each dwell of 10 s: from safe stop to creep, to reduced, to full.

questions.question: How far could the vehicle go on dead reckoning before its sigma reached 1.5 m?
options: As far as it likes: the gyro holds the heading
questions.explanation: The uncertainty grows as the root of the distance. From 0.05 m, at the growth the course measured, it reaches 1.5 m after 468 m, stepping the mode down on the way.
